children.text: brahmacārī vedam adhītyopanyāhṛtya gurave 'nujñāto dārān kurvīta ||
children.translated_text: A <s>brahmacārin</s> (Vedic student), after studying the Veda, presenting it to the teacher, and being permitted by the teacher, should take a wife.
And there is bathing.
Of those two rites, the bathing comes first.
But the mantra-recitation and formal salutation before the hand-taking have been explained previously.

children.text: brāhmaṇas sahodakumbhaḥ prāvṛto vāgyato 'greṇāgniṃ gatvodaṅmukhas tiṣṭhet ||
children.translated_text: A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, with a water-pot, covered and restraining speech, should go in front of the fire and stand facing north.

children.text: snātām ahatenācchādya yā akṛntann ity ānīyamānāyāṃ pāṇigrāho japet somo 'dadad iti ||
children.translated_text: When she has bathed, he should clothe her in an unworn garment; as she is being led forward with the verse beginning "yā akṛntan," the bridegroom should murmur the verse beginning "somo 'dadat."
He should seat her to the right of the bridegroom.
When she has touched him from behind, he should offer ghee with the great utterances, using the ladle for the preliminary portion.
With all of them together he should offer a fourth oblation.
The same procedure applies at the rites of first tonsure, initiation, and shaving the beard.

children.text: agnir etu prathama iti ṣaḍbhiś ca pāṇigrahaṇe ||
children.translated_text: At the hand-taking he should also use the six verses beginning "agnir etu prathamaḥ."
In ghee-offerings, unless there is a special instruction, there are no two portions of ghee and no offering to <s>Agni Sviṣṭakṛt</s>.
Everywhere, afterwards, he should offer with the great utterances.
And with the verse addressed to <s>Prajāpati</s>.
He should offer an expiatory oblation.
After offering, the two stand up.
Going behind her, he should stand on her right side and take the bride's joined hands.

children.text: pūrvā mātā śamīpalāśamiśrāl lājāñ chūrpe kṛtvā ||
children.translated_text: First the mother, having placed parched grain mixed with śamī and palāśa leaves in a winnowing basket, should stand there.

children.text: paścād agner dṛṣatputram ākramayed vadhūṃ dakṣiṇena ||
children.translated_text: Behind the fire he should make the bride step with her right foot on the upper millstone.

children.text: sakṛd gṛhītam añjaliṃ lājānāṃ vadhvañjalāv āvaped bhrātā prapadenemam aśmānam iti ||
children.translated_text: Her brother should pour once-taken handfuls of parched grain into the bride's joined hands with the front of his foot, while reciting "imam aśmānam."
Or some friend may do it.

children.text: taṃ sāgnau juhuyād avicchidyāñjaliṃ iyaṃ nārīti ||
children.translated_text: She should offer it into the fire, not breaking the joined hands, with the verse beginning "iyaṃ nārī."
For the next two offerings he uses the verses beginning "aryamaṇam" and "pūṣaṇam."

children.text: hute tenaiva gatvā pradakṣiṇam agniṃ pariṇayet kanyalā pitṛbhya iti ||
children.translated_text: When the offering has been made, he should go by that same path and lead her around the fire clockwise with the verse beginning "kanyalā pitṛbhyaḥ."
Beginning with the standing, he performs this same sequence three times.

children.text: śūrpeṇa śiṣṭān agnāv opya prāgudīcīm utkramayet ekam iṣa iti ||
children.translated_text: Having thrown the remaining grains from the winnowing basket into the fire, he should make her step toward the northeast with "ekam iṣe."
The looking at the axle-hole, mounting the chariot, and addressing difficult places are performed with suitable verses.

children.text: apareṇāgnim audako gatvā pāṇigrāhaṃ mūrdhany avasiñcet ||
children.translated_text: A water-carrier, going to the west of the fire, should sprinkle the bridegroom on the head.
And the bride as well.
After being sprinkled, he recites the verse beginning "samañjantu."

children.text: dakṣiṇaṃ pāṇiṃ sāṅguṣṭhaṃ gṛhṇīyāt gṛbhṇāmi ta iti ṣaḍbhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: He should take her right hand together with the thumb, using the six verses beginning "gṛbhṇāmi te."
He should lead her away toward the northeast.

children.text: brāhmaṇakule 'gnim upasamādhāya paścād agner lohitaṃ carmānaḍuham uttaraloma prāggrīvam āstīrya vāgyatām upaveśayet ||
children.translated_text: In a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> household, after placing the fire, he should spread behind the fire the red hide of a bull, with the hair upward and the neck toward the east, and seat her on it, silent.

children.text: prokte nakṣatre 'nvārabdhāyāṃ sruveṇopaghātaṃ juhuyāt ṣaḍbhir lekhāprabhṛtibhis sampātān avanayan mūrdhani vadhvāḥ ||
children.translated_text: When the prescribed asterism has been announced and she has touched him from behind, he should make offerings with the ladle and preliminary portion, using the six verses beginning with "lekhā," letting the drops fall upon the bride's head.

children.text: pradakṣiṇam agniṃ parikramya dhruvaṃ darśayati dhruvādyaur iti ||
children.translated_text: Having circumambulated the fire clockwise, he shows her the pole-star with the verse beginning "dhruvā dyauḥ."
After saluting the elders by clan-name, he should release speech.
A cow is the sacrificial fee.
Here an arghya offering is made.
Some say that it is when they have arrived.

children.text: trirātraṃ kṣāralavaṇe dugdham iti varjayantau saha śayīyātāṃ brahmacāriṇau ||
children.translated_text: For three nights the couple should sleep together as <s>brahmacārins</s>, avoiding alkaline substances, salt, and milk.

children.text: haviṣyam annaṃ parijapyānnapāśenety asāv iti vadhvā nāma brūyāt ||
children.translated_text: He should consecrate sacrificial food with the verse beginning "annapāśena," saying the bride's name in the place of "asau."
After eating, he should give the remainder to the bride.

children.text: ūrdhvaṃ trirātrāc catasṛbhir ājyaṃ juhuyāt agne prāyaścittir iti samasya pañcamīṃ sampātān avanayann udapātre ||
children.translated_text: After the three nights, he should offer ghee with four verses beginning "agne prāyaścittiḥ," combining the fifth, and should let the drops fall into a water-vessel.
With that water he should bathe her, hair and nails included.
After that, he may proceed according to the purpose.

children.text: ṛtukāle dakṣiṇena pāṇinopastham ālabhed viṣṇur yoniṃ kalpayatv iti samāptāyām ||
children.translated_text: At the fertile season, when it has ended, he should touch her generative organ with his right hand, reciting "viṣṇur yoniṃ kalpayatu."
He should have intercourse with her, reciting "garbhaṃ dhehi."
The new- and full-moon sacrifices are begun with the full moon.
If the new-moon rite comes first, he should sacrifice with the full-moon rite and then perform that one.
Some say that one who does not perform it should wait for the full-moon day.
In the afternoon, after bathing, the husband and wife should eat the fast-day food.

children.text: mānatantavya uvāca śreyasīṃ prajāṃ vindate kāmyo bhavatyakṣodhukī kṣodhuko ya aupavasathikaṃ bhuṅkte ||
children.translated_text: <s>Mānatantavya</s> said: One who eats the fast-day food obtains better offspring, becomes desirable, is not hungry; hungry is the one who eats the fast-day food.
Therefore he should eat whatever he desires.
He should not perform anything contrary to the vow.
In the morning, after offering the oblation,

children.text: havinirnirvapedamuṣmai tvā juṣṭaṃ nirvapāmīti devatāśrayaṃ sakṛdyajurvā dvistūṣṇīm ||
children.translated_text: he should set out the oblation, saying, "For so-and-so I set you out, acceptable," referring to the deity; once with a <s>yajus</s> formula, or twice silently.
He should rinse it three times for the gods.
Twice for human beings.
Once for the ancestors.
With the stirring-stick he should cook it clockwise until it has risen up.
When it is cooked, he should sprinkle it with ghee, set it down toward the north, and sprinkle it again.
All oblations are prepared in this same way.
After placing it on the sacred grass,

children.text: ājyabhāgau juhuyāccaturgṛhītamājyaṃ gṛhītvā pañcāvattaṃ bhṛgūṇāṃ jāmadagnyānāmagnaye svāhetyuttarataḥ somāyeti dakṣiṇataḥ ||
children.translated_text: he should offer the two ghee-portions, taking ghee in four ladlings and the fivefold portion: for the <s>Bhṛgus</s>, the <s>Jāmadagnyas</s>, to <s>Agni</s>, svāhā, on the northern side; to <s>Soma</s>, on the southern side.
For the others the order is reversed.
Having spread ghee beneath, he should cut a portion from the oblation with the stirring-stick, from the middle and from the front, as prescribed.
And afterwards there is the fivefold portion.
Having sprinkled with ghee, he anoints again the places from which portions were cut.
There is no such portion for <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s>.
He should offer with "to so-and-so, svāhā," according to whatever deity it belongs to.

children.text: sviṣṭakṛtaḥ sakṛd upastīrya dvirbhṛgūṇāṃ sakṛddhaviṣo dvirabhighāryāgnaye sviṣṭakṛte svāheti prāgudīcyāṃ juhuyāt ||
children.translated_text: For <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s>, after spreading ghee once beneath, taking twice for the <s>Bhṛgus</s>, once from the oblation, and sprinkling with ghee twice, he should offer toward the northeast with "to <s>Agni Sviṣṭakṛt</s>, svāhā."
He should place a fuel-stick on the fire.

children.text: darbhānājye haviṣi vā triravadhāyāgramadhyamūlānyaktaṃ rihāṇā viyantu vaya ityabhyukṣyāgnāvanumahared yaḥ paśūnāmadhipatī rudrastanticaro vṛṣā paśūnasmākaṃ mā hiṃsīretadastu hutaṃ tava svāheti ||
children.translated_text: Having placed darbha grass three times in the ghee or oblation, and having anointed its tip, middle, and root, he should sprinkle it with the verse, 'May they depart, licking,' and should offer it into the fire with approval, saying, 'Rudra, lord of cattle, who moves among them, the bull: do not harm our cattle. Let this be your oblation. Svāhā.'
That is the sacrificial site.
He should do this in every case.
Having carried the remainder of the oblation northward, he should give it to the brahman priest.
A full vessel is the dakṣiṇā (priestly fee).
Or else according to his ability.
For one who has not established the sacred fires, the pot-cooked offering at the new- and full-moon rites belongs to Agni.
For one who has established the fires, at the full moon it belongs to Agni and Soma.
At the new moon it belongs to Indra, or to Mahendra, or to Indra and Agni.
Or it may be as for one who has not established the sacred fires.
The whole day is the proper time for a morning oblation.
The night is the proper time for an evening oblation.
The whole dark fortnight is the time for the full-moon rite.
The bright fortnight is the time for the new-moon rite.
Some say that he should maintain continuity by abstaining from food.
When there is no oblation available, he should offer the fruits of sacrificial trees.
Or palāśa leaves.
Or water.
For it has been offered.
There is an expiation for what has not been offered.
When no particular oblation is prescribed, he should offer ghee.
When no particular mantras are prescribed, the deity is the guide.
In the third month of the first pregnancy, the <s>puṃsavana</s> (rite for male offspring) is performed.
After she has bathed, he should clothe her in a fresh garment, make an offering, and the husband should stand behind her.

children.text: dakṣiṇam aṃsam anvavamṛśyānantarhitaṃ nābhideśam abhimṛśet pumāṃsāviti ||
children.translated_text: Touching her right shoulder and then touching the region of the navel without anything intervening, he should say, 'May male offspring be born.'

children.text: athāparaṃ nyagrodhaśuṅgām ubhayataḥphalām asrāmām akrimiparisṛptāṃ triḥsaptair yavaiḥ parikrīyotthāpayenmāṣairvā sarvatrauṣadhayaḥ sumanaso bhūtvā 'syāṃ vīryaṃ samādhatteyaṃ karma kariṣyatīti ||
children.translated_text: Then he should take a downward-growing shoot of a banyan, with fruit on both sides, not diseased and not crawled over by worms, purchasing it all around with thrice seven barley grains, or with beans, saying, 'All herbs, having become well-disposed, place vigor in this woman for the rite that she is about to perform.'
Having brought it, he should make it suspended in the air.

children.text: kumārī brahmacārī vratavatī vā brāhmaṇī peṣayedapratyāharantī ||
children.translated_text: A maiden, a celibate student, or a vow-observing Brahmin woman should grind it, without turning back.
Having made the bathed woman sit, he should pour it into the right nostril, saying, 'Agni is male.'
Then, in her fourth month or sixth month, comes the <s>sīmantonnayana</s> (parting of the hair).

children.text: snātāmahatenācchādya hutvā patiḥ pṛṣṭhatastiṣṭhannanupūrvayā phalavṛkṣaśākhayā sakṛtsīmantamunnayet triśvetayā ca śalalyā 'yamūrjāvato vṛkṣa iti ||
children.translated_text: After she has bathed, he should clothe her in a fresh garment, make an offering, and, standing behind her, part her hair once in due order with a branch of a fruit-bearing tree, and also with a three-white-spotted porcupine quill, saying, 'This tree is full of nourishment.'
Kṛsara is the pot-cooked offering.
While she is looking at the upper ghee, he should ask her, 'What do you see?'
He should make her say, 'Offspring.'
When the dwelling is established, the oblation for a woman about to give birth is performed.
With the two verses beginning 'She who crosswise ...'.
He should give the name, saying, 'So-and-so.'
That is secret.
Before cutting the navel-cord and before giving the breast, he should grind rice and barley enclosed with shoots.
Taking it with his thumb and ring finger, he should make the boy eat it, saying, 'This is command.'
And ghee, with the formula, 'May it give you understanding.'

children.text: jananāj jyautsne tṛtīye tṛtīyāyāṃ prātaḥ snāpya kumāram astamite astamite śāntāsu dikṣu pitā candramasam upatiṣṭhet upatiṣṭhet prāñjaliḥ ||
children.translated_text: On the third lunar day in the bright fortnight after birth, in the morning, having bathed the boy, at each sunset when the quarters are quiet, the father should worship the moon, standing with joined hands.
The mother, having clothed him in a clean garment, should hand him over with his head toward the north.
Going behind him, she should stand to the north.
She should stand.

children.text: yat te te susīma iti tisṛbhir upasthāyodañcaṃ upasthāyodañcaṃ upasthāyodañcaṃ upasthāyodañcaṃ mātre pradāya yad ada ada ity apām apām añjalim añjalim avasiñcet ||
children.translated_text: Having worshipped with the three verses beginning 'What of yours, O well-bounded one,' facing north, repeatedly facing north according to the text, and having handed him to the mother, he should pour out handful after handful of water with the formula, 'What, what of this.'
He should pour it out.
Twice silently.
Silently.

children.text: jananād ūrdhvaṃ ūrdhvaṃ daśarātrāc chatarātrāt saṃvatsarād vā nāma kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: After birth, after ten nights, after a hundred nights, or after a year, he should perform the naming.

children.text: snāpya kumāraṃ kariṣyata upaviṣṭasya śucinācchādya mātā prayacched udakśirasam ||
children.translated_text: Having bathed the boy, the mother should clothe him in a clean garment and hand him over, with his head toward the north, to the seated man who is about to perform the rite.
Going behind him, she should sit to the north.

children.text: hutvā ko'sīti tasya mukhyān prāṇān abhimṛśet ||
children.translated_text: After making an offering, with 'Who are you?' he should touch the chief vital breaths of the child.
He should touch them.

children.text: asāv iti iti nāma kuryāt tad tad eva eva mantrānte ||
children.translated_text: Saying, 'So-and-so,' he should give the name; that very name is to be inserted at the end of the mantra.
To the mother.
Having first announced it.
Having announced it.

children.text: viproṣyaṅgād aṅgād aṅgād iti iti putrasya mūrdhānaṃ parigṛhṇīyāt ||
children.translated_text: On returning from abroad, with the formula 'From limb to limb,' he should take hold of his son's head.
With 'Of cattle I smell you,' he should smell him.
He should smell him.
For a female, silently.
In the third year, the <s>caula</s> (tonsure) is performed.

children.text: tatra nāpita uṣṇodakam ādarśaḥ ādarśaḥ kṣuro vaudumbaraḥ piñjūlya iti dakṣiṇataḥ ||
children.translated_text: There, the barber, hot water, a mirror, a razor, or an udumbara implement, and darbha bunches are to be placed on the south side.

children.text: ānaḍuho gomayaḥ kṛsaras sthālīpāko sthālīpāko vṛthāpakva ity uttarataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Dung of an ox, kṛsara, and the pot-cooked offering, cooked casually, are to be placed on the north side.
On the north side.
And the mother, taking the boy.
Taking him.

children.text: hutvā 'yam āgād āgād iti iti nāpitaṃ prekṣet savitāraṃ savitāraṃ dhyāyan ||
children.translated_text: After making an offering, he should look at the barber with the formula 'This one has come, has come,' meditating on <s>Savitṛ</s>.

children.text: uṣṇenety uṣṇodakaṃ uṣṇodakaṃ uṣṇodakaṃ uṣṇodakaṃ prekṣed vāyuṃ vāyuṃ dhyāyan ||
children.translated_text: With 'By the warm one,' he should look at the hot water, repeatedly as the text has it, meditating on <s>Vāyu</s>.
With 'The waters,' he should moisten him.
He should moisten him.

children.text: viṣṇor ity ity ādarśaṃ ādarśaṃ prekṣed audumbaraṃ audumbaraṃ vā ||
children.translated_text: With 'Of <s>Viṣṇu</s>,' he should look at the mirror, or at the udumbara implement.

children.text: oṣadha iti darbhapiñjūlīs saptordhvāgrā saptordhvāgrā saptordhvāgrā saptordhvāgrā saptordhvāgrā saptordhvāgrā abhinidhāya ||
children.translated_text: With 'O herb,' having placed seven darbha bunches with their tips upward, as repeated in the text.

children.text: svadhita ity ādarśena ādarśena kṣureṇaudumbareṇa vā ||
children.translated_text: With 'O axe,' using the mirror and the razor, or the udumbara implement.

children.text: yena pūṣeti dakṣiṇatas triḥ triḥ prāñcaṃ prohet ||
children.translated_text: With the verse beginning 'With which <s>Pūṣan</s>,' he should comb forward three times from the right side.

children.text: sakṛd āyasena āyasena pracchidyānaḍuhe gomaye keśān kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: Cutting once with an iron implement, he should place the hairs on the dung of an ox.

children.text: undanaprabhṛty undanaprabhṛty undanaprabhṛty undanaprabhṛty evaṃ evaṃ paścād uttarataś uttarataś ca ||
children.translated_text: Beginning with the moistening, beginning with the moistening, in just this way, afterward and to the north and to the north.
And.

children.text: tryāyuṣam iti iti putrasya mūrdhānaṃ parigṛhya japet ||
children.translated_text: Saying “threefold life,” he should murmur the formula while taking hold of his son’s head.
Having moved upward toward the north, he should perform the welfare rite according to the rule of his gotra and family.
According to the rule of his gotra and family.
They should bury the hair in the forest.
They should bury it.
Some place it on a post.
Some.
A cow is the sacrificial fee.
The sacrificial fee.
He should initiate a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> in the eighth year.
He should initiate him.
The time for him has not passed until the sixteenth year.
A <s>Kṣatriya</s> in the eleventh year.
For him, until the twenty-second year.
A <s>Vaiśya</s> in the twelfth year.
For him, until the twenty-fourth year.

children.text: kuśalīkṛtam alaṃkṛtam alaṃkṛtam ahatenācchādya ahatenācchādya ahatenācchādya ahatenācchādya hutvāgne vratapata iti ||
children.translated_text: Having made him ritually well, adorned him, and clothed him in an unworn garment, he should sacrifice with the formula “O <s>Agni</s>, lord of vows.”

children.text: uttarato 'gneḥ pratyaṅmukham avasthāpyāñjaliṃ avasthāpyāñjaliṃ avasthāpyāñjaliṃ avasthāpyāñjaliṃ kārayet ||
children.translated_text: He should station him north of the fire, facing west, and cause him to form an añjali.
He himself should place his own hands above.

children.text: dakṣiṇatas tiṣṭhan tiṣṭhan mantravān mantravān brāhmaṇa ācāryāyodakāñjaliṃ pūrayet ||
children.translated_text: Standing on the south, a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> who knows the mantras should fill an añjali of water for the teacher.
While the boy is looking on, he should murmur, “You have come here.”

children.text: ko nāmāsīty ukto ukto devatāśrayaṃ nakṣatrāśrayaṃ vā 'bhivādanīyaṃ nāma brūyād asāv asāv asmīti ||
children.translated_text: When asked, “What is your name?”, he should state the name to be used in respectful greeting, based on a deity or on a lunar mansion, saying, “I am so-and-so.”
“I am.”
“I am.”
“I am.”

children.text: utsṛjyāpo devasya ta iti dakṣiṇottarābhyāṃ hastābhyām añjaliṃ añjaliṃ gṛhṇīyād ācāryaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having released the water, the teacher should take the añjali with both hands, south and north, with the formula “Of the god, to you.”
The teacher.
With the formula “Of the sun,” he should turn him clockwise.
He should turn him.

children.text: dakṣiṇam aṃsam aṃsam anvavamṛśyānantarhitāṃ anvavamṛśyānantarhitāṃ anvavamṛśyānantarhitāṃ anvavamṛśyānantarhitāṃ nābhim ālabhet ālabhet prāṇānām prāṇānām iti ||
children.translated_text: Having touched down along his right shoulder, without anything intervening, he should touch his navel with the formula “Of the breaths.”
Thus.
Then he should hand him over with the formulas beginning with “Antaka.”
With the formulas beginning with “Antaka.”
The right shoulder with the formula “To <s>Prajāpati</s>, you.”
With his left hand, the left shoulder, with the formula “To the god, you.”
“You are a brahmacārin.”
“You are.”
“You are.”
“You are.”

children.text: saṃpreṣyopaviśya dakṣiṇajānvaktam añjalikṛtaṃ añjalikṛtaṃ añjalikṛtaṃ añjalikṛtaṃ pradakṣiṇaṃ muñjamekhalām ābadhnan ābadhnan vācayed vācayed iyaṃ iyaṃ duruktād iti ||
children.translated_text: Having instructed him, seated him with the right knee bent and hands joined, he should tie the muñja girdle clockwise and make him recite the formula beginning “This one from evil speech.”
Thus.
He should approach, saying, “Teach me, sir.”
He should approach.

children.text: tasmā anvāha sāvitrīṃ paccho 'rdharcaśas sarvām sarvām iti iti sāvitrīṃ vācayet ||
children.translated_text: To him the teacher recites the <s>Sāvitrī</s>; he should make him recite the <s>Sāvitrī</s> by quarters, by half-verses, and as a whole.
And the great vyāhṛtis, one by one.
And one by one.
And one by one.
And one by one.
And the syllable <s>oṃ</s>.
He gives him a wooden staff.
With the formula “May good fame, good fame, come to me.”

children.text: samidham ādadhyād ādadhyād agnaye agnaye samidham iti ||
children.translated_text: He should place a fuel-stick on the fire with the formula “For <s>Agni</s>, a fuel-stick.”
Thus.
He should go for alms.
First to his mother.
First.
Then to other well-wishers.
Well-wishers.
He should present the alms to the teacher.
He should stand silently until sunset.
Silently.
For three nights he should avoid pungent substances, salt, and milk.
At the godāna rite the procedure is as at the caula.
The procedure.
He should have it shaved together with the hair.
Cows, horses, and pairs of sheep are the separate sacrificial fees for the different varṇas.
Or a cow may be the fee for all.
A goat is for receiving the hair.
The upanayana has been stated.
The upanayana.
He should not undertake observances for a year if he is not going to practice them.
But if he is not assigned, he should be in an unworn garment.
Unworn.
Likewise with adornment.
He should lie down below.
He should not eat honey or meat.
He should avoid sexual intercourse, shaving, bathing, anointing, cleaning the teeth, and washing the feet.
His semen should not spill at will.
Should spill.
He should not mount anything yoked with cows.
He should mount.
He should not wear sandals in the village.
Wearing the girdle, begging for alms, carrying the staff, placing fuel-sticks, sipping water, and morning salutation are constant duties.
The godāna vow, the vrātika vow, the Āditya vow, the Upaniṣad vow, and the Jyeṣṭhasāmika vow last for a year.
They last for a year.
For some, there is no Āditya vow.
For some.

children.text: ye caranty ekavāsaso ekavāsaso ekavāsaso ekavāsaso bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: Those who observe it wear a single garment.
And they do not place anything between themselves and the sun.
Nor do they go near water.

children.text: śakvarīṇāṃ dvādaśa nava ṣaṭ traya traya iti vikalpāḥ ||
children.translated_text: For the Śakvarī verses, the alternatives are twelve, nine, six, and three.
He wears black clothing.
He eats black food.
He is dependent on the teacher.
He should stand by day.
By day.
He should sit at night.

children.text: saṃvatsaram ekeṣāṃ ekeṣāṃ pūrvaiḥ śrutāś cet ||
children.translated_text: For some, it lasts a year, if the earlier authorities so taught.
If.
For one who has fasted, with his eyes bound, he should cause the recitation to follow.

children.text: yathā mā na pradhakṣyatīti taṃ prātar abhivīkṣayanti abhivīkṣayanti yāny apradhakṣyantaṃ apradhakṣyantaṃ manyante 'po 'gniṃ vatsam ādityam ||
children.translated_text: In the morning they show him those things which they think will not burn him, saying “So that it may not burn me”: water, fire, a calf, and the sun.
The sun.

children.text: apo 'bhivyakhyam ity ity apo apo jyotir abhivyakhyam abhivyakhyam ity ity agniṃ agniṃ paśūn abhivyakhyam abhivyakhyam iti iti vatsaṃ sur abhivyakhyam abhivyakhyam ity ity ādityaṃ ādityaṃ visṛjed vācam ||
children.translated_text: Saying, 'I have beheld the waters,' he should release speech after beholding the waters, the light, Agni, the cattle, the calf, and the sun with the repeated formulae.
Speech.
A cow is the dakṣiṇā (honorarium).
The honorarium.
Or a bronze vessel, a garment, and a gold ornament.
And.

children.text: anupravacanīyeṣv ṛcaṃ ṛcaṃ sāma sadasaspatim iti iti cājyaṃ juhuyāt ||
children.translated_text: At the anupravacanīya offerings he should offer ghee with each ṛc and sāman, and also with the verse beginning 'sadasaspati'.

children.text: cityayūpopasparśanakarṇakrośākṣivepaneṣu sūryābhyuditas sūryābhinirmukta sūryābhinirmukta sūryābhinirmukta sūryābhinirmukta indriyaiś ca ca pāpasparśaiḥ punar mām mām ity ity etābhyām etābhyām āhutiṃ āhutiṃ juhuyāt ||
children.translated_text: When touching a piled altar-post, hearing with the ear, or twitching of the eye occurs, he should offer an oblation with the two formulae beginning 'risen with the sun' and 'freed from the sun ... restore me with the senses and from evil contacts'.
Or on a fuel-stick smeared with ghee.

children.text: japed vā vā laghuṣu japed vā vā laghuṣu ||
children.translated_text: Or he may mutter the formula in minor cases; or he may mutter it in minor cases.
For the bathing rite he sits beforehand, enclosed, in front of the teacher's house.
The teacher faces north, on kuśa-grass whose tips point east.
In this way acts one who desires brahmavarcas, sacred brilliance.
In a cow-stall acts one who desires cattle.
In an assembly acts one who desires fame.
He should make the waters foam with all herbs.
And with fragrant substances.
With those waters, neither too cold nor too hot, the teacher should sprinkle him.
Or he may do it himself after saluting the mantras.

children.text: ubhāv ity eke tenemam ity ācāryo brūyāt ||
children.translated_text: Some say that both do it; with the formula beginning 'with this man', the teacher should speak.

children.text: ye apsv ity apām añjalim avasiñcet ||
children.translated_text: With 'ye in the waters' he should pour down a handful of water.
And also with 'what is of the waters'.
And silently.
Taking water with 'he who is the shining one', he should sprinkle himself.
And with 'with which a woman'.
And silently.
With 'rising up' he should attend upon the sun.
Or he may combine the recitations.
While moving about, he should draw it together with 'you are sight'.
With 'up, the highest' he should loosen the girdle.
After eating, he should have the hair of the head, beard, body-hair, and nails cut, except for the topknot.
Adorned and wearing an unworn garment, with 'splendor' he should put on a garland.
With 'you are guides' he should put on the sandals.
He should take up a bamboo staff with 'you are a Gandharva'.
Approaching the teacher, he should look at the assembly with 'like a yakṣa'.
Sitting down, with 'covering of the lips' he should touch the principal vital breaths.
He should touch a cart yoked with cows with 'O tree'.
With 'your rider' he should mount it.
He should set out eastward or northward and turn round clockwise.
Some say that, when he has returned, an arghya is to be offered.
From then onward he should be of mature conduct.
He should not desire intercourse in jest with a girl before her body-hair has appeared.
Nor with one not joined to him in proper marriage.
Nor with a menstruating woman.
Nor with a woman of the same ṛṣi-lineage.
He should not eat food entered by another door, twice-cooked food, or food kept overnight.
Except preparations of vegetables, meat, barley, and flour.
And milk-rice as well.
He should not gather fruit, look into a well, run in the rain, or carry his sandals himself.
He should not wear an unscented garland, unless it is a gold garland.
He should not utter the word 'auspicious' in vain.
One desiring prosperity should wash the cows with 'these are mine'.
When they have returned, he should say, 'these honey-sweet ones'.

children.text: puṣṭikāma eva prathamajātasya vatsasya prāṅ mātuḥ pralehanāl lalāṭam ullihya nigiret gavām iti ||
children.translated_text: One desiring prosperity should lick the forehead of the first-born calf before its mother licks it and swallow the saliva, with the formula beginning 'of the cows'.

children.text: saṃprajātāsu goṣṭhe niśāyāṃ vilayanaṃ juhuyāt saṃgraheṇeti ||
children.translated_text: When the cows have calved, at night in the cow-stall he should offer the vilayana oblation with 'with gathering'.

children.text: athāparaṃ vatsamithunayoḥ karṇe lakṣaṇaṃ kuryāt bhuvanam iti ||
children.translated_text: Then, on another occasion, he should make a mark on the ear of a pair of calves with 'the world'.
First on the male.
He should consecrate it with 'with the red one'.
A cord is stretched out with 'this cord'.
